tasks.short: Replenish mail equipment consumables and check that equipment runs correctly.

steps.what: Inspect consumable levels and identify the required replacement.
Isolate equipment as instructed, then refill reservoirs or replace cartridges and ribbons.
Run a test piece and check print, seal, or feed quality.

tasks.design: Configure reminders and consumable reorder thresholds in the {WORKFLOW}, with maintenance instructions linked from the {DOCS}. The clerk still replenishes equipment and tests it; reminders only reduce avoidable inspections and shortages.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most effort is physical handling. Software cannot refill a reservoir or replace a ribbon.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reminders and simple stock records are inexpensive to configure. AI coding can shorten setup, but does not change the physical work.
tasks.still_hard: Equipment varies, counters may be unavailable, and poor seals or feed problems need hands-on diagnosis.
tasks.human_edge: Notice leaks, wear, unusual resistance, and unsafe conditions before restarting equipment.
tasks.altitude: The week changes little. Fewer shortages are possible, but replenishment and equipment readiness remain the clerk's responsibility; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Plan preventive maintenance for shared office equipment.
reach.learn: Service intervals, fault escalation, and consumable stock thresholds.

evidence.claim: Replenishment and test-piece inspection remain physical work; reminders provide only limited assistance.
Build ranges and remaining-time estimates are planning assumptions, not measured results.

assumptions: Existing mail equipment remains in service.
The clerk may perform routine replenishment under equipment instructions.
Time shares represent active work, excluding equipment downtime.
The design records equipment status rather than individual worker performance.
unknowns: Equipment models, consumable types, and available level counters.
Existing reminder capabilities and access permissions.
Applicable national rules on employee consultation.
research_questions: Can existing counters trigger reminders without a custom connection?
Would a simple minimum-stock rule prevent the common shortages?
new_work: Maintain consumable thresholds and reminder intervals.

tasks.short: Weigh outgoing mail, select postage, and apply and check stamps or meter impressions.

steps.what: Weigh and measure outgoing items and identify destination and required service.
Select tariff, service, and cost centre in the {OTHER} postage equipment controls.
Feed items through the meter or physically attach the required postage.
Check postage placement and legibility, separating spoiled or incorrect items for correction.

tasks.design: Configure approved tariffs, service defaults, and cost centres in the {OTHER} postage equipment controls. Where supported, connect weight input and retain transaction records; the clerk checks the selected service, handles the items, and inspects impressions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical handling dominates, while tariff entry and cost coding depend on equipment capabilities.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing equipment settings may remove repeated selections. Small deterministic connections are cheaper to build where interfaces already exist.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed item sizes, unusual destinations, poor impressions, and incompatible equipment limit savings.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise unsuitable packaging, sensitive documents, and service requirements that the dispatch request leaves unclear.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes into tariff selection and repeated entry. Physical preparation remains most of the task, and spending authority does not change.

reach.task: Prepare parcels against carrier acceptance requirements.
reach.learn: Packaging standards, size limits, service classes, and dispatch cutoffs.

evidence.claim: Existing postage equipment can support tariff settings and weighing; exact capabilities depend on installed equipment.
Software assistance leaves feeding, affixing, and visual inspection largely physical.
Build ranges and remaining-time estimates require local validation.

assumptions: Existing equipment supports tariff and service defaults.
Required physical mail remains physical; electronic delivery needs separate sender agreement.
Postage-setting approval occurs before postage is applied.
GDPR applies to recipient data; EU AI Act obligations depend on any AI actually introduced.
unknowns: Equipment interfaces, weighing capability, and tariff-update arrangements.
Volumes, item mix, and proportion already processed automatically.
Cost-centre coding requirements and postage spending limits.
research_questions: Which repeated selections can existing settings remove?
Does connecting the scale save enough handling time to justify integration?
new_work: Check tariff updates and service defaults.
Resolve failed weight transfers and incorrect default selections.

tasks.short: Explain mailing and shipping policies and resolve questions about permitted services.

steps.what: Receive the question and clarify destination, item type, urgency, and sender needs.
Find current policy, carrier restrictions, and service guidance in the {DOCS}.
Resolve requests outside published policy and authorise any exception.
Explain the answer and next steps to the requester.

loop.input: Clarified inquiry, retrieved approved guidance, and any authorised policy ruling.
loop.output: Short answer with source references and next steps.
loop.check: Require current sources for policy claims; validate dates and limits; clerk approves before delivery.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction maximum; missing or conflicting support returns the inquiry to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard questions; varied free-text questions need a bounded drafting step.

tasks.design: Configure a structured inquiry form and searchable policy collection in the {HELPDESK} and {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts answers from approved guidance for clerk review, while the {WORKFLOW} sends policy exceptions to the facilities manager before the answer is delivered.
tasks.previous_blocker: Guidance is scattered, changes over time, and rarely matches the wording of an employee's question.
tasks.enabler_now: Search, forms, and approval routing already cover most of the work. A bounded drafting loop can turn retrieved guidance into a clear answer.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting guidance, restricted items, unusual destinations, and requests for policy exceptions still need accountable judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the sender's actual need and explain practical alternatives when the requested service is unsuitable.

ambition.what: Searchable mailing guidance for employees outside mailroom opening hours.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time searching and repeating explanations, and more time resolving unusual requests. Publishing approved guidance expands service access; policy exception authority stays with the facilities manager.

reach.task: Maintain employee guidance for shared office services.
reach.learn: Policy publishing, accessible instructions, source ownership, and review intervals.

evidence.claim: An answer desk using approved policy text, with unknowns escalated to a person, is a feasible design.
Search and structured questions can handle routine guidance without an autonomous agent.
The digest provides no documented mailing-policy answer-desk case; build and time estimates remain assumptions.

assumptions: Questions commonly arrive by telephone or at the mailroom; email is another channel.
Manager consultation is an exception path; its share is averaged across the task.
Approved guidance may be published for employee self-service.
Standard templates are used before model drafting.
GDPR applies to inquiry records; EU AI Act duties depend on the deployed system and use.
unknowns: Which role can approve policy exceptions.
Guidance quality, languages, and update ownership.
Actual inquiry channels and exception frequency.
Whether inquiries contain recipient or shipment information requiring restricted access.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing access permissions.
research_questions: What proportion of recent inquiries can a short decision tree answer?
Can the current {HELPDESK} provide policy search and routing through configuration?
Which question types should always reach a person?
new_work: Review drafted answers and unsupported claims.
Maintain policy versions, search terms, and standard responses.
Turn recurring questions into approved self-service articles.

tasks.short: Select a suitable courier service, book collection, and share delivery details.

steps.what: Collect addresses, parcel details, collection window, deadline, and cost centre from the requester.
Check available services and prices in the {PARTNER_PORTAL} against the delivery requirement.
Approve exceptional cost, urgency, or service conditions before booking.
Enter shipment details and confirm collection through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}.
Send collection instructions, labels, and tracking details to the requester.

tasks.design: A validated form in the {WORKFLOW} captures shipment requirements, and a deterministic integration checks contracted services through the {PARTNER_PORTAL}. It books requests within delegated limits, waits for facilities-manager approval on exceptions, and sends labels and confirmation through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incomplete requests, repeated portal entry, and separate approval messages make a simple booking process labour intensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured forms, rule-based service selection, and supported carrier interfaces can remove coordination work. AI coding reduces connection-building effort where interfaces exist.
tasks.still_hard: Unsupported carrier interfaces, failed collections, customs requirements, and unusual items still need intervention.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate a workable recovery when a collection fails or no standard service meets the sender's deadline.

ambition.what: Proactive recovery coordination for missed courier collections.

tasks.altitude: Routine booking gives way to monitoring failed collections and arranging recovery. The clerk can gain authority to choose an alternative contracted service within an agreed recovery budget.

reach.task: Compare collection reliability and recovery options across contracted services.
reach.learn: Service commitments, exception causes, alternative routes, and total shipment cost.

evidence.claim: Structured intake and deterministic carrier connections can automate routine courier bookings where supported interfaces exist.
Booking needs validation, duplicate prevention, and exception handling; an autonomous agent is unnecessary.
The digest provides no courier-booking implementation case; build and remaining-time estimates require local validation.

assumptions: Contracted carriers provide supported booking interfaces.
Most requests concern ordinary domestic or regional letters and parcels.
The organisation delegates routine booking authority within defined limits.
Manager approval applies only to exceptions; its time share is averaged across requests.
Booking retries check the existing booking reference before creating another shipment.
GDPR applies to address data; EU AI Act obligations depend on any AI actually introduced.
Expanded recovery authority requires explicit delegation before use.
unknowns: Carrier interface access, fees, and cancellation rules.
Existing booking tools and automation capabilities.
International, restricted-item, and customs shipment volumes.
Availability of collection-status events for proactive recovery.
research_questions: Can existing {PARTNER_PORTAL} settings handle booking and notifications without custom code?
Which service rules reliably distinguish routine bookings from exceptions?
How will booking outcomes be reconciled after a connection timeout?
new_work: Resolve invalid addresses, unavailable services, and failed bookings.
Maintain carrier credentials, service rules, and spending limits.
Reconcile uncertain booking outcomes and prevent duplicates.
Monitor missed collections and arrange authorised recovery.

role.altitude: Physical replenishment and postage handling remain central. Administrative time shifts toward policy exceptions, equipment readiness, and failed-collection recovery; any new spending rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Facilities manager: preventive maintenance and service continuity.
Administrative services manager: policy guidance and employee self-service.
Logistics analyst: carrier reliability and shipment recovery.
skills_to_grow: Configure forms, service defaults, and approval rules.
Validate carrier records and resolve duplicate or uncertain bookings.
Handle recipient data with appropriate access and retention.
role.ambitious_version: Become an office dispatch coordinator who keeps physical mail moving, publishes usable guidance, and resolves collection failures within an explicitly delegated recovery budget.

job.title: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
